title: Gambhir Sets 'Mission 300' After India's Afghanistan T20I Rout
excerpt: India's head coach says the team's first 100-run powerplay of his tenure matters more than Abhishek Sharma's century — and 300 is the next target.
body:
• India completed a 3-0 T20I whitewash of Afghanistan with a 127-run win in Delhi on September 17, powered by Abhishek Sharma's 108 off 34 balls.
  • Head coach Gautam Gambhir named India's first 100-run powerplay of his tenure the team's biggest positive — ahead of the century itself.
  • Gambhir set "Mission 300" as the next frontier, saying: "We still haven't reached 300. That's probably the next target, because the kind of talent we have in the dressing room, we should be doing some incredible things."
  • The reigning T20 world champions have a best of 297-6, set against Bangladesh in Hyderabad in October 2024.

India crushed Afghanistan by 127 runs in the third T20I at the Arun Jaitley Stadium in Delhi on Thursday, sealing a 3-0 series whitewash. But the scoreboard was not what head coach Gautam Gambhir wanted to talk about afterward. Instead, he announced a new obsession: Mission 300.

Asked about the win, Gambhir brushed past Abhishek Sharma's blistering 108 off 34 balls and Sanju Samson's 50 off 35, calling India's 100 in the powerplay — the first time the side has crossed that mark under his watch — the standout achievement. "We still haven't reached 300," he said. "So that's probably the next target, because the kind of talent we have in the dressing room, we should be doing some incredible things."

"We still haven't reached 300. That's probably the next target, because the kind of talent we have in the dressing room, we should be doing some incredible things."

— Gautam Gambhir, India head coach

A new bar for a champion side

The ambition is not empty talk. India are the reigning T20 World Cup champions, having beaten New Zealand by 96 runs in the final at Ahmedabad on March 8 to claim their third T20 title — the first team in history to do so. The victory capped a run of three successive ICC crowns, following the 2024 T20 World Cup and the 2025 Champions Trophy.

This year, India also became the first T20 side to score four 250-plus totals in a calendar year. Thursday's 221-7 against Afghanistan was another exhibition: sent in to bat, India were carried by Sharma's 108 off 34, with Samson adding 50 off 35. Afghanistan, set 222, were dismissed for 94 in 14.1 overs.

The philosophy behind the chase

For Gambhir, the 300 mark is the logical extension of an ideology he has preached since taking the job: that T20 cricket is measured in impact, not aggregates. "It's not about the 100 that he scored today. I can sit here and keep talking about his hundred, but it's just the impact," he said of Sharma. "The only thing that we talk about in that dressing room is how much impact can we create with the bat and how much impact can we create with the ball."

"T20 cricket is not about runs or wickets, it's about how much impact you can create," he added. The message to the squad, he said, is simple: "If you're going hard, just keep going hard."

"T20 cricket is not about runs or wickets, it's about how much impact you can create."

— Gautam Gambhir

The 300 chase and the road to it

No team has ever crossed 300 in a T20 international. India's current best is the 297-6 they posted against Bangladesh in Hyderabad in October 2024 — agonisingly short of the landmark. Gambhir has been explicit about it since the World Cup: "We haven't touched 300 yet, but we aim to, and our goal is to become even more ruthless," he said earlier this year on Star Sports.

The same press conference offered a window into the coach's harder calls. Gambhir admitted that leaving Sanju Samson out of the playing eleven during the England series was "probably the toughest decision I've taken in my coaching tenure," adding that selection comes down to form and the team's impact-first ethos.

Why it matters beyond the boundary

For the Indian diaspora, which turns out in enormous numbers wherever India play, this is the most entertaining Team India in memory — a side that treats bilateral series not as warm-ups but as record-hunting missions. The T20 game was an English invention; India is now its standard-bearer, and the chase for 300 would be another first planted in Indian colours.

What to watch next

India's white-ball calendar continues at home, and every high-scoring track is now a potential stage for the 300 chase. If the powerplay template from Delhi — 100 inside six overs — becomes the norm rather than the exception, the record could fall sooner than anyone expects. Gambhir's players have been told exactly what is expected: keep going hard.
